dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you this morning?

Good morning, Mr. Kevin. Thank you for answering. My name is Carmela Barone. I am calling about the water in the street, the drain, in front of my house. It is a big problem, and it is not the first time.
Okay, sorry to hear that. Let me get some details. What's the address?
Yes. Forty-eight Rhode Island Avenue, in the Historic Hill. I rent there, I am the tenant, but I am the one who sees it every day.
Forty-eight Rhode Island Avenue. Got it. And this is from the rain over the weekend?

Yes, the rain from Friday into Saturday, two days ago. The street in front of the house turned into a pond, a real pond. The water does not go down. It stays and stays. And the cars, they come fast and they throw the water like waves, like a boat, you understand? The wake goes up to the steps.
Wow, okay. So the drain out front isn't taking any water, it sounds like.

No, nothing. I looked from the window on Saturday morning and it was full, the water all the way across. I think the drain is blocked with leaves, with dirt, I do not know. Somebody must clean it, no? That is why I call.

Yeah, that'd be the catch basin. Let me jot this down. Catch basin at forty-eight Rhode Island Avenue, standing water across the roadway after Friday-Saturday rain, vehicles throwing wakes. Anything else you noticed? Is it up on the sidewalk too?

Yes, a little on the sidewalk, at the edge. And I must tell you also, there is an older neighbor next door, a lady, she is very old, she uses a walker. On Saturday she could not get out of her door. She wanted to go to the pharmacy and she could not cross, it was too much water. That worries me, because if she needs an ambulance, what happens?
Right, that's a good point to put in the notes. Access for an elderly neighbor. I'll flag that.
Thank you. Please, put it. And I want to ask you something. When did they come last? The city, the people who clean the drains. Do you have a record of when they last came to this street?

Let me see what I've got here. [pause] Hmm, I'm pulling up the street. I'm not seeing a recent cleaning entry for that block in what's in front of me. That doesn't mean nobody was there, it might just be logged somewhere else. I can ask the drain crew supervisor to check.

So you do not see anything. Hm. For me, it looks like nobody comes. I walk every morning to my office, and I read everything, every sign, every notice on the poles, because it is my habit, I cannot help it. And I never see a notice about cleaning the drains on my street. Never one.
Okay, so you'd have noticed. Street sweeping signs and so on, those are different from the drain cleaning, but I hear you. Nothing posted that you've seen.
Nothing. And every time it rains hard, the same. I am sorry to say, but it feels like the city forgets this street.

I understand why it feels like that. Let me do this properly. I'll put in a work order for the crew to inspect and clear the catch basin out front of forty-eight, and I'll mark it as a repeat problem since you're saying it happens every heavy rain. Is that fair?
Yes, it is fair, it happens every heavy rain. Not only this one. Please write that.
Writing it. Repeat ponding, every heavy rain. Now, is the water still there today, or has it drained down some?

Today it is less. The sun came out yesterday and this morning there is only a little water by the curb. But it is not because the drain works, it is because the water goes away slowly by itself. The drain is still the same, I think.
Okay. Still worth having them look, because the next rain it'll just do it again. Can I get a number in case the supervisor needs to reach you?
Yes, of course. It is four-zero-one, five-five-five, zero-one-eight-eight. This is my house phone, the landline.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-eight. Perfect. And it's Barone, B-A-R-O-N-E?
Yes, correct. Carmela Barone. Two R? No, one R. B, A, R, O, N, E.
Got it, one R. Thanks, Ms. Barone.
Mr. Kevin, may I ask, when will they come? I do not want to be impolite, but I have asked myself this many times, and I would like to tell my neighbor something.

Totally fair. After a storm like this the crews are working through a pile of calls, so I'd say give it the next several days, maybe into next week. Given the access issue with your neighbor, I'll note it as a higher priority so it doesn't sit.
Next week. Hm. That is long if it rains again on Wednesday. But I understand, you are many calls. If it rains before, and the street is like a pond again, I can call again?

Absolutely, call right back and give them the work order information, and we'll add it to the file. If the water's ever deep enough that it's a safety problem, like someone can't get out and needs help, that's a call for emergency services, not us.
Yes, yes, I understand. I hope not. She is a very nice lady, a little stubborn, she does not like to ask for help.
Well, hopefully the crew gets out there before the next one. Anything else I can note for them? Any landmark, a hydrant or a telephone pole by the drain?
The drain is at the edge of the street, directly in front of my steps, a little to the left if you look at the house from the street. Near the tree, a small tree with a fence around it.
Perfect, in front of the steps, left side, by the little tree. That'll help them find it.
Thank you. You are very kind, Mr. Kevin. I hope this time somebody comes.
I'll make sure it's in the queue with all that detail. You have a good Monday, Ms. Barone.
You also. Thank you very much. Goodbye.
Bye now.
